PUBLIC COMMENT
Citizens wishing to address the City Council and Successor Agency on any item on the agenda or on any matter
not on the agenda may do so at this time. State law (Government Code Section 54950 et seq.) prohibits the City
Council from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda .
Upon request, the City Council may, in their discretion, allow citizen participation on a specific item on the agenda
at the time the item is considered by the City Council. If you wish to address the City Council /Successor Agency
at this time, please complete a speaker's card and give it to the City Clerk prior to commencement of the City
Council meeting. Please limit your remarks to three (3) minutes.

To increase the effectiveness of the Public Comment Period, the following rules shall be followed: No person shall
make any remarks which result in disrupting, disturbing or otherwise impeding the meeting.

Pursuant to Section 54957.95 of the Government Code, the presiding member of the legislative body conducting a
meeting, or their designee, is authorized to remove, or cause the removal of, an individual for disrupting the
meeting. Any such removal will be preceded by a warning to the disruptive individual by the presiding member of
the legislative body or their designee that the individual ’s behavior is disrupting the meeting and that the individual ’s
failure to promptly cease their disruptive behavior may result in their removal.

  CONSENT CALENDAR
Items under the Consent Calendar are considered to be routine and may be enacted by one motion. There will be
no discussion of these items unless members of the Public or City Council request specific items to be removed
from the Consent Agenda for a separate discussion. lf the item is desired to be discussed separately, it should be
the first item under Scheduled Matters.

Proclamation Declaring March 21, 2024, as World Down Syndrome Day Director of Parks and Recreation Alaniz conducted a presentation, introducing commissioners, Club 21 participants, and parents.Director Alaniz advocated for the wearing of quirky socks on March 21, 2024, symbolizing the celebration of uniqueness and fostering inclusivity. PUBLIC COMMENT Gloria Nezahualcoyotl urged the City Council to reassess the allocation of funds for senior programs, ensuring their effective utilization. She emphasized the need for programs to align with their intended purposes. Additionally, Nezahualcoyotl requested accommodations for seniors residing far from the nearest bus stops on the Blue and Red routes.




CONSENT CALENDAR  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Kevin Lainez Councilmember Rebollo requested to pull item #5 for discussion, and Councilmember Garcia requested to pull items #6, and #7. 
Item #5 – Councilmember Rebollo raised concerns regarding potential leaks following the completion of roof repairs. Noting that the interior ceiling still exhibited signs of leakage despite the roof repair, Councilmember Rebollo questioned why the interior issue had not been addressed. In response, Director of Parks and Recreation Alaniz clarified that the responsibility for ceiling repairs fell under the jurisdiction of the Public Works staff.

Additionally, Councilmember Rebollo asked staff to repair the ceiling at Bandini Park as soon as possible. Councilmember Garcia inquired regarding the final inspection process for project completion, to which Director Alaniz emphasized the collaborative effort among departments. When asked about timelines for addressing ceiling repairs and other related issues, Director Alaniz indicated that such requests would be handled by the Public Works Department, with prioritization based on urgency and efficiency.

Assistant City Manager Domic assured that staff would conduct another walkthrough to address any deficiencies, with any additional funding needs to be addressed during the Capital Improvement Program (CIP) budget presentation.

Mayor Argumedo recommended tabling the item to the next meeting due to the identified deficiencies and potential leaks. The City Council reached a consensus to postpone further discussion on the matter.

Item #6 – When Councilmember Garcia inquired about the allocation of Proposition A Funds, Assistant City Manager Vilko clarified that although these funds have not been utilized directly, the money received would serve to address gaps within the Transportation department.

Councilmember Rebollo moved, seconded by Councilmember Lainez, to adopt the Resolution approving a Fund Trade Agreement for the exchange of Proposition A funds with the City of El Segundo. The motion was carried by the following vote:

AYES: Councilmembers Garcia, Lainez, Rebollo, Vice Mayor Altamirano and Mayor Argumedo (5)

Item #7 –In reply to Councilmember Garcia's inquiries regarding the city's obligation to approve the final design at present, Transportation Director McFerguson confirmed that indeed, the city is obligated to do so, even if the decision is made not to proceed with the project.

Vice Mayor Altamirano moved, seconded by Councilmember Lainez, to adopt a Resolution to approve the Fifth Amendment to the Professional Service Agreement between the City of Commerce and Stantec Architecture Incorporated for architecture and engineering services. The motion was carried by the following vote:

AYES: Councilmembers Garcia, Lainez, Rebollo, Vice Mayor Altamirano and Mayor Argumedo (5)

Consideration of Purchase and Installation of Outdoor Fitness Equipment at Rosewood Park through Sourcewell Cooperative Agreement with BCI Burke Company Director of Parks and Recreation Alaniz delivered a presentation highlighting the deterioration of current equipment and emphasized that all expenses would be covered by Measure A Los Angeles County funds. According to Direcotr Alaniz, the location chosen was based on minimal use of the area, no trees relocation needed, and less impactful to the remaining of the park. Moreover, he noted the planned connectivity with the Pathway of Hopes.

Councilmember Garcia raised concerns about utilizing green space. She suggested exploring alternative sites near the basketball courts by the EOC to mitigate this concern.

Discussion ensued regarding the suitability of various locations, considering noise levels and space constraints, including the potential need to remove trees. In response to Councilmember Garcia's inquiry about maintenance, Director Alaniz assured that the equipment carries a 20-year warranty.

Councilmember Rebollo advocated for prioritizing a project at Bristow Park, citing its worse condition compared to Rosewood. Director Alaniz countered that Rosewood sees greater equipment usage, and the City could apply for more funds from Measure A could be allocated for Bristow Park.

Councilmember Lainez highlighted the proximity of the proposed site to the Senior Center, anticipating increased utilization. This aligns with the Parks Master Plan's goal of promoting fitness and a healthy lifestyle.

Consideration was given to the current use of the location for soccer overflow games. Vice Mayor Altamirano suggested installing rubber flooring for safety, but Director Alaniz cautioned against it due to cost and maintenance concerns.

Mayor Argumedo suggested utilizing existing equipment location and retaining existing trees within the project area and relocating younger trees to another park. Mayor Argumedo emphasized the safety benefits of rubber flooring and proposed adding a hard roof to prolong equipment lifespan.

Further discussion centered on preserving trees and green space, as well as exploring alternative locations, such as behind the EOC. Director Alaniz noted the noise generated by basketball and the importance of visibility. Councilmember Garcia requested additional analysis and options for presentation at a future City Council meeting.

Consequently, the item was deferred to a future meeting for further deliberation.

CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS Councilmember Garcia expressed her heartfelt condolences to the Barragan family for their loss of Lupe Barragan.

Councilmember Lainez also extended condolences to the Barragan family. Additionally, he shared his participation in Read Across America and thanked the deputies from the Sheriff’s Department who took part. Councilmember Lainez reported attending various events including the Commerce Business Council Installation Dinner, a Clippers Game event, and expressed gratitude to Frank Garcia and other staff for their efforts in organizing these events for Commerce residents. He also mentioned attending all five performances of Unplugged Juniors' production of Aladdin and congratulated Amber Torres on her upcoming role as Supervisor of the Teen Center. Furthermore, Councilmember Lainez asked to agendize a review of approved and funded job positions that remain unfilled.

Councilmember Rebollo echoed condolences to the Barragan family and reported attending similar events as Councilmember Lainez. She suggested exploring the possibility of renting a theater for Unplugged productions and commended Public Safety Manager Edson for his social media efforts regarding enforcement, including addressing vehicles obstructing roadways and sidewalks. Councilmember Rebollo recommended amending the municipal code to allow residents to create parking spaces on their front lawns to address parking issues.  

Vice Mayor Altamirano agreed on the importance of discussing parking issues and recognized Sonia, the Library Director, for her creativity on library programs.

Mayor Argumedo shared his attendance at Clippers events, the Commerce Business Council Installation Dinner, and a quarterly Mayor's meeting with the Business Council. He concurred with the need to review the Municipal Code, suggesting options such as permit parking or implementing T-marks. Additionally, Mayor Argumedo conveyed his condolences to the Barragan family.


ADJOURNMENT Meeting adjourned at 8:39 p.m. in memory of Lupe Barragan.

8.. Presentation/Update from the Sheriff's Department of Public Safety in the City of Commerce Sergeant Duarte presented statistics covering the month of February through March 8th.

Councilmember Rebbollo expressed gratitude to Sergeant Duarte and the Deputies for their dedicated efforts. She inquired about specialized training for deputies in handling individuals with special needs. Sergeant Duarte affirmed that they undergo training through the mental health foundation annually. Councilmember Rebbollo advocated for increased partnerships and collaboration with organizations like Club 21.

Councilmember Lainez highlighted the significance of the railroad in Commerce and expressed concerns about deputies' allocation of resources and time towards addressing railroad-related issues instead of focusing on residential areas. Sergeant Duarte explained that Union Pacific's response to issues is often delayed. Following further discussion, Councilmember Lainez requested that staff communicate with Union Pacific and BNSF to ensure the allocation of resources for maintaining cleanliness in those areas.

Mayor Argumedo noted the passage of Proposition 1 and expressed interest in understanding its impact on the city and how to secure resources for Commerce.
